blocks.h2: Signs Your Water Heater Needs Repair
blocks.intro: Most water heater problems give you a warning first. Here's what to watch for:

tiles.h3: No Hot Water, or Not Enough
tiles.body: A pilot that won't stay lit, a failed element or thermostat, or a tank full of sediment can all cut your hot water short.
A small leak at a valve or fitting is often a repair. Water coming from the tank itself usually means the tank has failed.
Sediment builds up on the bottom of the tank and crackles as the burner heats through it. It's a sign the tank needs flushing, or is near the end.
Rust-colored water or a rotten-egg smell from the hot tap points to a corroding tank or a worn anode rod.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Problems in Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: The median Highland Park home was built in 1963. Water heaters don't last that long, so most homes here are on their second, third or fourth heater, installed around older plumbing.

items.body: In a Lake County winter, the water coming into your home is much colder, so the heater works harder to keep up. That's when a struggling heater usually gives out, often on the coldest night of the year.
When a heater does need replacing, the new one has to meet today's code for venting, gas and water connections, even if the old one didn't. We'll tell you up front if your setup needs changes.

If the repair costs a big share of a new unit, or the tank itself is leaking, replacement usually makes more sense. See [water heater installation](/highland-park/water-heater-installation) or, if you're considering an upgrade, [tankless water heaters](/highland-park/tankless-water-heater).

bodies: We service the water heaters found in Highland Park homes: gas and electric tank heaters, tankless units, and heaters installed in basements, utility rooms and garages. Repair, replacement, flushing and safety checks all start the same way: a technician looks at your heater before recommending anything.

Not sure what you have? The label on the side of the tank lists the fuel type, capacity and manufacture date. Tell us what it says when you call and we'll come prepared. For a new heater, see [water heater installation](/highland-park/water-heater-installation).

Sediment settles to the bottom of every tank. Over time it makes the heater work harder, creates rumbling noises and shortens the life of the tank. Flushing the tank clears that sediment out. Checking the anode rod, the pressure relief valve and the burner or elements catches wear before it turns into a leak or a cold shower.

Most manufacturers recommend flushing a tank heater about once a year. Tankless units need regular descaling. If your heater is rumbling, slow to heat or has never been flushed, a maintenance visit is a good first step before a repair.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Should I repair or replace my water heater?
items.preview: A leaking tank means replace. A failed part on a younger heater usually means repair.
items.answer: If the tank itself is leaking, it needs replacing. If it's a part like a thermostat, element, igniter or valve, a repair usually makes sense, especially on a heater under 8 to 10 years old. If the repair would cost a big share of a new unit, we'll tell you, and you decide.

items.q: What is the life expectancy of a water heater?
items.preview: Tank heaters typically last about 8 to 12 years. Tankless units often last longer.
items.answer: Tank water heaters typically last about 8 to 12 years. Tankless units often last longer with regular descaling. Sediment, water quality and how hard the heater works in winter all affect lifespan.

items.q: Why is my water heater leaking from the bottom?
items.preview: It's either a valve, which is a repair, or the tank, which means replacement.
items.answer: It can be a drain valve or relief valve that's dripping, which is a repair, or the tank itself corroding through, which means replacement. Turn off the water supply to the heater and call. We'll tell you which one it is.

items.q: How much does water heater repair cost in Highland Park?
items.preview: It depends on the failed part and heater type. You get a flat price before any work begins.
items.answer: It depends on what's failed, the heater type and the parts it needs. We diagnose first and give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in.

items.q: How often should a water heater be serviced?
items.preview: About once a year for a tank flush. Tankless units need regular descaling.
items.answer: Most manufacturers recommend flushing a tank heater about once a year and descaling tankless units regularly. An annual check also catches a worn anode rod or a sticky relief valve early. See [water heater maintenance](#water-heater-maintenance).
